clue.text: Agreed there's no time to open the wine

indicators.note: no time means the letter for time is dropped, here from the front of the wine as 'to open' says

parts.note: Tokay is a sweet Hungarian dessert wine

explanation.surface: Someone concedes that there is no time left to uncork the bottle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'no' with 'to open' takes T from the start of TOKAY, leaving the reply.
explanation.definitionFit: Saying a casual yes to a proposal is the same as having consented.

clue.text: Humpty Dumpty's downfall was so unexpected

explanation.surface: The nursery-rhyme egg's tumble came as a great surprise.
explanation.walkthrough: Humpty Dumpty sat on a wall and had a great fall, so his downfall was literally from that spot; the phrase also means bizarre.
explanation.definitionFit: The egg tumbled from his perch on the brickwork; colloquially the phrase means eccentric or surprising.

clue.text: Girl picks engagement rings up

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the run is read from bottom to top, backwards
the phrase picks engagement encircles a run of letters, which it rings round

explanation.surface: A young woman chooses the jewellery for her betrothal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rings' marks the letters SENGA sitting inside 'picks engagement'; 'up' turns them round.
explanation.definitionFit: A common female first name, so an example of a girl.

clue.text: At end of alley, see principal London sight

indicators.note: the principal piece comes at the end of the alley piece in the charade

parts.note: an alley is a large playing marble, often of real stone
arch as an adjective means chief or principal, as in arch-villain

explanation.surface: Standing at the end of a lane, you can spot the capital's chief landmark.
explanation.walkthrough: MARBLE ARCH is a white triumphal arch at the west end of Oxford Street in London; an alley is the old name for a choice playing marble.
explanation.definitionFit: A monumental gateway near Hyde Park, a well-known tourist landmark in the capital.

clue.text: Sailor, disgraced, avoided port?

parts.note: AB, able-bodied seaman, is a standard abbreviation for a sailor
a stained reputation is one that has been disgraced

explanation.surface: A seaman in disgrace kept away from the harbour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'port' looks like a harbour for the sailor, but it is the fortified wine; the question mark flags that refusing a drink is meant.
explanation.definitionFit: To refrain from drinking the fortified wine is to have declined it, the teetotal sense.

clue.text: Jazz musician beats time regularly

indicators.note: regularly means taking every other letter of beats time, starting with the first

explanation.surface: A jazz drummer keeps steady rhythm.
explanation.walkthrough: Count Basie was an American jazz bandleader and pianist.
explanation.definitionFit: Count Basie led one of the great swing bands as pianist, so he is a famous example.

clue.text: Old pilot's terribly daring feat

parts.note: ex- means former, so old

indicators.note: terribly signals the letters of pilot jumbled into a new order

parts.note: the 's only shows possession or stands for 'is', so it adds no letters: the word before it gives these letters as it is written

explanation.surface: A veteran airman pulls off an awfully bold stunt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Old' reads as describing the pilot, but it gives the prefix meaning former; 'terribly' is the anagram signal on the pilot.
explanation.definitionFit: A bold or heroic deed is called a feat or an adventure of this kind.

clue.text: There's something fishy about daughter's hairstyle

parts.note: re means about or concerning
D is the abbreviation for daughter in family trees
a mullet is a haircut short at front and long at the back

explanation.surface: Something seems suspicious about a girl's haircut.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fishy' suggests suspicion, but the definition is literal: an edible sea creature.
explanation.definitionFit: A prized red-skinned food species from the sea, literally a thing that is a fish.

clue.text: Call to dog to secure ball

explanation.surface: A trainer commands the pet to grab the ball.
explanation.walkthrough: In rugby a hooker heels the ball back in the scrum, winning possession.
explanation.definitionFit: It is the command that brings a pet to walk at your side; in a rugby scrum to backheel the ball wins it.

clue.text: Wartime charge, importing new snack from abroad?

indicators.note: importing means the attack word takes another letter inside it

parts.note: a blitz is a sudden military attack, as on London in 1940

explanation.surface: A wartime bombing campaign brings in a novel foreign dish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'importing' puts N inside BLITZ.
explanation.definitionFit: A thin Jewish pancake from Eastern Europe, a foreign dish eaten as a light meal.

clue.text: Successful cup team at home in football association sets of fixtures

indicators.note: in means the at-home word goes inside the association's initials

parts.note: FA, the Football Association, governs English football
in means at home, as in staying in
fixture lists are the schedules of matches

explanation.surface: A winning cup side plays at home within the governing body's match schedules.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Successful cup team' is a fair definition: a side reaching the final has succeeded in every earlier round. 'at home' gives the first 'in'; the second 'in' is the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A side that has won through to the last match of a knockout tournament has been successful.

clue.text: Fatso, say, is back after school

indicators.note: after means the reversed piece is placed after the school piece

parts.note: a pod is a school of whales or dolphins

indicators.note: back means the abbreviation for say is written backwards

parts.note: e.g. means for example, so say

explanation.surface: A fat boy returns to his classmates after lessons.
explanation.walkthrough: 'school' suggests a classroom, but it is a group of whales; 'back' turns EG to GE.
explanation.definitionFit: An informal, mocking name for a plump person, like a chubby or fatty.

clue.text: At sea, Noah's suppressing an exclamation of joy

indicators.note: suppressing means holding down, so the jumble keeps the word an inside it
at sea means confused, so the letters of Noah's are mixed up

parts.note: the letters of the name with its s

explanation.surface: Noah, adrift on the flood, holds back a cry of delight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'At sea' fits Noah's ark on the flood, but it signals a jumble of his name with its s; 'suppressing' then holds the word an inside the jumble, giving HOSNA around AN.
explanation.definitionFit: A shout of praise and adoration used in Christian worship.

clue.text: Book departure

explanation.surface: A two-word clue pairing a volume with a leaving.
explanation.definitionFit: The second book of the Old Testament; also a mass leaving.

clue.text: Northern town fighting with distinction

parts.note: warring means fighting or at war
ton is fashionable style or distinction, as in bon ton

explanation.surface: A town in the north is fighting with honour.
explanation.walkthrough: WARRINGTON is a large town in Cheshire, north-west England.
explanation.definitionFit: A town in north-west England between Liverpool and Manchester, so a northern one.

clue.text: Australian version of dancing queen we nearly had once?

parts.note: waltzing is dancing a waltz
Empress Matilda, daughter of Henry I, was his chosen heir but lost the English throne to Stephen

explanation.surface: Refers to a famous Abba hit and an Australian rendering of it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dancing queen' calls up the Abba song, but it splits into two words. Matilda never reigned, so England nearly had her as queen; the song is Australia's unofficial anthem.
explanation.definitionFit: The bush ballad serves as an unofficial anthem for Australians, their own national song.

clue.text: Wobbly top? Prop needed

parts.note: something wobbly is loose
the head is the top of something

explanation.surface: A top is wobbling, so a support is wanted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Prop' looks like a support, but it is a rugby position: the loosehead prop packs down on the left of the front row of the scrum.
explanation.definitionFit: In rugby union the front-row forward on the left of the scrum is called this kind of prop.

clue.text: Rocky terrain in camp, so one is unsettled

indicators.note: unsettled means disturbed, so the letters of camp so one are rearranged

explanation.surface: A camp on rough ground leaves one feeling uneasy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is unsettled' rearranges CAMPSOONE.
explanation.definitionFit: A lunar-like landscape of bare rock and craters is a barren, stony terrain.

clue.text: Former actor starred in solo parts in front of the queen

indicators.note: parts means the words starred in solo are broken into pieces and reassembled

parts.note: ER, Elizabeth Regina, stands for the Queen, with the jumble placed in front of it

explanation.surface: A past actor took the lead in a one-man show before the monarch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'parts' rearranges STARREDINSOLO; ER follows. LEONARD ROSSITER (died 1984) was a British comic actor, star of the sitcom Rising Damp.
explanation.definitionFit: A British comic star of the 1970s who died in 1984, so a performer of the past.

clue.text: Begin to deal with speech

explanation.surface: Starting to tackle a speech.
explanation.definitionFit: To tackle a problem is to start handling it; a formal talk to an audience is also so called.

clue.text: Influenced kid when speaking

indicators.note: when speaking means the word for the leather is heard rather than read

parts.note: kid is soft leather, and suede is leather of that sort

explanation.surface: A child was persuaded by what was said.
explanation.walkthrough: 'kid' looks like a child, but it is leather; SUEDE said aloud matches the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To have been persuaded or moved by someone is to have been swung their way.

clue.text: One joining with church official

parts.note: an elder is a lay officer in Presbyterian churches

explanation.surface: Someone becoming a member alongside a church officer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One joining' reads as a new member, but it is a tradesman fusing metal.
explanation.definitionFit: A tradesman who fuses metal parts together with heat is literally a joiner of pieces.

clue.text: Crew member given reprimand about standing up

parts.note: a row is a telling-off

indicators.note: in a down clue, standing up means the word for about is read upwards, backwards

parts.note: re means about or concerning

explanation.surface: A crewman gets a telling-off for being upright.
explanation.walkthrough: 'standing up' turns RE to ER.
explanation.definitionFit: A member of a boat crew who pulls an oar, as in the Boat Race.

clue.text: Substitute's reputation no good

definitions.note: read as substitute is, the 's being a link

indicators.note: no good means the letter for good is dropped

parts.note: standing means status or reputation

explanation.surface: A replacement player's reputation is worthless.
explanation.walkthrough: 'no good' removes G from STANDING.
explanation.definitionFit: A person who takes another's place temporarily, such as an understudy, is a replacement.

clue.text: Two singers leading mass at old cathedral

indicators.note: leading means the pair comes before the other pieces

parts.note: a duo is a pair of performers
M is the abbreviation for mass in physics

explanation.surface: A pair of vocalists lead the service at an ancient church.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mass' suggests the church service, but it is the physics symbol M. A DUOMO is an Italian cathedral.
explanation.definitionFit: The Italian word for a city's principal church, as in Florence's famous dome.

clue.text: Prophet first to be expelled from Aegean island

indicators.note: the first letter of the island is thrown out

parts.note: Samos is a Greek island in the eastern Aegean

explanation.surface: A holy man is the first to be thrown off a Greek island.
explanation.walkthrough: 'first to be expelled from' takes S off SAMOS.
explanation.definitionFit: A minor Old Testament seer with his own book of the Bible.

clue.text: Bull you twice noticed near entrance to meadow

indicators.note: near means the doubled word sits next to the opening letter
the entrance to a word is its first letter
twice means the word for you is written two times

parts.note: ye is an old form of you

explanation.surface: A bull is spotted in a field by the gate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bull' looks like a field animal, but it means nonsense; 'noticed' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are exclamations of disbelief, slang for nonsense or rubbish.

clue.text: Surprised exclamation, landing extremely large creature in sailing vessel

indicators.note: landing as with a catch, so the exclamation takes the other pieces inside it

parts.note: what! is a cry of surprise

indicators.note: extremely means the first and last letters of large

parts.note: a boa is a snake, a creature

explanation.surface: A startled cry as a huge animal is hauled into a boat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'large creature' looks like the whale itself, but splits: 'extremely' takes the first and last letters of large, and 'landing' puts them and the snake inside the cry of surprise.
explanation.definitionFit: A long narrow rowing or sailing boat once used in hunting, a type of craft.

clue.text: Way factions negotiate noisily

indicators.note: noisily means the words for factions and negotiate are heard aloud

parts.note: sides are factions in a dispute; to treat is to negotiate, as in treat with the enemy

explanation.surface: Opposing groups bargain loudly.
explanation.walkthrough: SIDES TREAT, said aloud, sounds like the minor road.
explanation.definitionFit: A minor road off a main one is a thoroughfare, a kind of route.

clue.text: Noddy in short trousers

indicators.note: short means the word for trousers loses its last letter

parts.note: loons are flared trousers fashionable in the 1970s

explanation.surface: A simpleton wearing shorts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'short trousers' suggests shorts. A noddy is a fool; loons are flared trousers.
explanation.definitionFit: Both mean a silly person, a fool or simpleton.
